policies.title: Korean nationals: Korean-passport entry rather than foreign visa process
policies.summary: A person with Korean nationality must use a Korean passport to enter and leave the Republic of Korea and does not need K-ETA on that passport.
conditions: This citizenship classification does not establish document requirements for a particular carrier or a dual national attempting to travel on a non-Korean passport.
The cited government guidance states that Korean nationality holders must use a Korean passport to enter and leave Korea.

policies.title: Temporary K-ETA exemption: listed passports with 90-day stay rule
policies.summary: The listed passport codes are temporarily exempt from the K-ETA requirement through 31 December 2026 (KST); the eligibility table gives a 90-day stay rule.
conditions: The temporary exemption is in force from 1 January 2026 through 31 December 2026 (KST).
The live eligibility table gives these codes an allowed period of stay of 90 days.
The exemption concerns K-ETA. A traveller may still apply voluntarily for K-ETA to receive its stated arrival-card benefit, for the fee.
GB is limited to the table’s UK British Citizen (GBR) entry; other British nationality documents appear separately in the table and are not established by the GB code.
This policy does not establish work, study, residence, diplomatic, official, transit, crew, or other special-document access.

policies.title: Listed passports: K-ETA route with 30-day stay rule
policies.summary: The listed passports may use the K-ETA pre-travel authorization route for visa-free short entry, subject to the listed stay rule.
conditions: The listed stay rule is 30 days.

Applies only to passport holders represented by the listed nationality or region codes in the live K-ETA eligibility table; it does not establish a rule for a passport nationality absent from that table.

The K-ETA route is for visa-free entry for tourism, visiting relatives, events or meetings, or business without profit-making activity; it does not establish work, study, residence, or other long-stay access.
K-ETA is not a visa and approval does not guarantee admission; a Korea Immigration Service officer makes the final entry decision.

The K-ETA eligibility table separately names British nationality documents. The GB code here is limited to the table’s UK British Citizen (GBR) entry; the table separately shows other British documents with 30-day stays.

The reviewed sources do not state an ePassport condition, so this candidate adds none. Diplomatic and official passports, United Nations passports, residence cards, valid visas, SOFA service members, crew, ABTC holders, transfer passengers, and the stated age groups have separate K-ETA treatment.
The Korea Visa Portal e-Visa facility is limited to stated statuses and applicants; it does not establish a general tourist e-Visa entitlement for every passport code in this policy.

application.label: Official Korea Electronic Travel Authorization (K-ETA) application
application.processingTime: The K-ETA guide says assessment typically takes 72 hours or less, but it may take longer.
steps: Confirm that the passport is in the official K-ETA eligibility table and that the trip is within the visa-free short-stay purpose.
Apply through the official K-ETA website before boarding a flight or ship.
Provide the required passport information, email address, photograph, and payment through the official process.
Travel only after approval; K-ETA validity is separate from the applicable visa-free stay period.
